texts.cpp.assignment.theory:
int energy = 20; creates an object with an initial value. energy = 12; changes an existing object. Assignment evaluates the right-hand side first, then stores the result on the left: energy = energy + 5; adds 5 to the previous value. It is not a mathematical equality.

The shorthand energy += 5; does the same for our integer variable. The operators -= and *= work similarly. After assignment, the old value is lost unless you saved it elsewhere. To exchange values, use a temporary variable: int saved = a; a = b; b = saved;. Names must start with a letter or underscore; for these exercises, choose clear Latin-letter names and avoid reserved naming patterns.
texts.cpp.assignment.title: Assignment and state

texts.cpp.branches.theory:
An if / else if / else chain checks conditions from top to bottom and executes only the first matching branch. Unlike independent if statements, it prevents repeated output. Start with conditions that must not be hidden by broader ones.

switch (code) selects a case label using an integer or character value. break exits the switch; without it, execution may continue into the following case. default handles other values. Use if for ranges and compound logic, and switch for individual codes. Here, break exits switch; its role in loops will be studied separately.
texts.cpp.branches.title: More than two alternatives

texts.cpp.conversion.summary: Do not lose the fraction before storing a double.
texts.cpp.conversion.theory:
An operation's result type is determined by its operands, not by the destination variable. double x = 5 / 2; stores 2.0 because integer division has already happened. Writing 5.0 / 2 or static_cast<double>(a) / b performs floating-point division. static_cast<double>(a) explicitly converts the value of a.

Converting double to int discards the fractional part towards zero, but is valid only when the resulting value is representable. Parentheses and casts must come before an operation that would lose the information you need. Do not conclude that double is always the most accurate type: different types have different purposes and limitations. The small integers in these tasks convert exactly to double.
texts.cpp.conversion.title: Conversions and limits

texts.cpp.dispatcher.theory:

This assessment uses no loops, functions or string variables: only the numbers, bool, input, arithmetic and branching already studied. Try extreme values, equality and conflicting rules. Do not add restrictions that the task does not specify.

texts.cpp.division.microscope: Integer division by zero is undefined behavior. It cannot be promised to produce a friendly error message or an exception. For signed integers, dividing the minimum value by −1 is also dangerous when the result is not representable. Such inputs are excluded from these tasks.

texts.cpp.division.recap: The integer quotient tells you how many full groups fit; the remainder tells you how much is left. Always check the allowed divisors.
texts.cpp.division.summary: Split cargo into full packages and a remainder.
texts.cpp.division.theory:
When both operands are integers, / performs integer division: 17 / 5 gives 3. The remainder operator % complements that division: 17 % 5 gives 2. For nonnegative a and positive b, a = (a / b) * b + a % b, and the remainder is between 0 and b-1.

For negative integers, the quotient is truncated towards zero: -17 / 5 is -3, and -17 % 5 is -2. This is not rounding down. Our packaging tasks use nonnegative numbers, so the everyday interpretation of a remainder applies. Neither / nor % may use a zero divisor. When a divisor is read, the task guarantees that it is positive.
texts.cpp.division.title: Division and remainder

texts.cpp.escapes.theory:
Inside a string literal, a double quotation mark ends the text. To print the quotation mark itself, write \". To print a backslash, write \\. The sequence \t represents a tab, but its visual width depends on where it is displayed; these tasks use ordinary spaces for exact alignment.

A // comment continues to the end of the source line and is not executed. A /* ... */ comment can span several lines. Inside quotation marks, // is just text. Do not hide the only required statements inside a comment.
texts.cpp.escapes.title: Quotes, backslashes and comments

texts.cpp.first.theory:
An algorithm is a finite sequence of steps that an executor can follow. A program expresses an algorithm in a programming language. C++ is case-sensitive: main and Main are different names.

An ordinary console program starts executing in int main(). Braces enclose its body. The statement std::cout << "Ready"; sends text to standard output. A semicolon ends the statement; quotation marks delimit the text and are not printed. The directive #include <iostream> makes input/output declarations available. For now, use this structure without trying to memorize every detail.

In codelib, you can write code, save it and compare it with a reference solution. There is no built-in execution yet. Do not confuse marking a task complete yourself with checking a program using a compiler.

texts.cpp.flow.summary: Stop a search and skip unwanted values.
texts.cpp.flow.theory:
break exits the nearest loop or switch. continue skips the remainder of the current iteration: in for, the step executes next, followed by the condition; in while, the condition is checked immediately. A misplaced continue can skip a while counter update and create an infinite loop.

In nested loops, the inner loop runs through its iterations for each outer value. For a table of rows lines and cols characters, the outer loop handles lines and the inner loop handles each line's contents. Print the newline after the inner loop.

When streaming a known number of values, do not stop reading early without a reason: if more data is needed afterwards, the unread values remain in the input stream.
texts.cpp.flow.title: break, continue and nesting

texts.cpp.for.summary: Repeat an action a known number of times.
texts.cpp.for.theory:
for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) { ... } creates a counter i, tests the condition before each iteration, and increments i after the body. With n=3, the body sees i equal to 0, 1 and 2. ++i increments the variable by one. For now, use increment as a separate step rather than inside complex expressions.

If the condition is false initially, the body executes zero times. A variable declared in the for header is available inside the loop, but not after it. To accumulate a sum, create sum=0 before the loop and add values inside. Do not reset sum on every iteration.

Plan output separators separately: if (i > 0) before a space can avoid a trailing space.
texts.cpp.for.title: The for loop

texts.cpp.if.microscope: A numeric value can be converted to bool in a condition: zero means false, and a nonzero value means true. Consequently, if (x = 5) may compile and behave differently from your intention. Use == for comparison and enable compiler warnings; do not memorize the incorrect rule that assignment in if is always a syntax error.
texts.cpp.if.recap: Test the value exactly on the boundary separately. = stores; == compares.
texts.cpp.if.summary: Perform different actions depending on a condition.
texts.cpp.if.theory:
if (condition) { ... } executes its block when the condition is true. else { ... } provides an alternative. The operators >, <, >=, <=, == and != compare values and return bool. Equality uses two signs, ==; a single = assigns a value.

Always put branches in braces: this makes statements easier to add and prevents confusion. Do not put ; immediately after if (...): that creates an empty statement instead of the intended block. You may omit else when no alternative is needed. Read the task carefully to decide which branch includes equality.
texts.cpp.if.title: Branching with if / else

texts.cpp.input.theory:
A variable is a named object that stores a value of a particular type. int count = 0; creates an integer variable named count with the initial value 0. Names are case-sensitive. std::cin >> count; reads an integer from standard input and stores it in count. You can read several numbers in a chain: std::cin >> price >> count;. Spaces and line breaks separate the numbers.

Do not use quotation marks when printing a variable: std::cout << count;. Writing "count" would print the word. The operators + and * add and multiply numbers. In this section, input is guaranteed to be valid and all results fit in int; we will study invalid input later. Do not print prompts such as "Enter a number" when the required output contains only the answer.

texts.cpp.lines.theory:
Statements execute in order, from top to bottom. Separate output operations join their text without adding spaces. To start a new line, put \n inside a string literal. For example, "A\nB" contains A, a line break and B. You can write std::cout << "A" << "B"; as one output chain.

Spaces and line breaks in the source file outside quotation marks usually format the code and are not printed. A line break in the output appears only when explicitly requested. These tasks show the required output; a final line break is acceptable when comparing results by hand, but an extra blank line changes the output.
texts.cpp.lines.title: Lines and sequence

texts.cpp.logic.summary: Combine requirements without copying mathematical traps.
texts.cpp.logic.theory:
&& means logical AND: both conditions must hold. || means OR: at least one must hold. ! changes true to false and vice versa. To check whether x belongs to [a,b], write a <= x && x <= b. The spelling a <= x <= b does not mean a range: it chains two separate comparisons with an intermediate bool.

&& and || short-circuit: the right-hand side of && is evaluated only when the left-hand side is true, and the right-hand side of || only when the left-hand side is false. This allows divisor != 0 && value % divisor == 0 to avoid division by zero. Parentheses around meaningful groups improve readability; ! has higher precedence than &&, which has higher precedence than ||.

texts.cpp.priority.summary: Turn a formula into an expression.
texts.cpp.priority.theory:
Multiplication * and division / have higher precedence than + and -. Parentheses change the grouping: (a + b) * c adds a and b first. Operators + and - at the same precedence level group from left to right: a - b - c means (a - b) - c.

Unary minus changes a value's sign: -x. Use named intermediate results to keep expressions readable. Do not rely on notation such as 2(a+b): C++ requires explicit multiplication, as in 2 * (a + b).

In this lesson, every intermediate integer result is between −30000 and 30000. This avoids overflow even on an implementation with the minimum required int range.
texts.cpp.priority.title: Expression grouping

texts.cpp.supplies.theory:
This assessment combines input, arithmetic, packaging and fractional results. Before writing code, check three cases: nothing is needed, division is exact, and a partial group remains. For n ≥ 0 and k > 0, (n + k - 1) / k gives the required number of boxes, provided that the addition does not overflow. In our tasks, n + k - 1 ≤ 10100.

This formula rounds nonnegative integer division up; it is not a universal rule for arbitrary signs. When the quotient represents a measurement, use floating-point division rather than the number of full packages.

texts.cpp.telemetry.microscope: An algorithm invariant is a statement preserved after every iteration. For a maximum, best equals the largest value read so far. Initialization from the first element makes this true before the loop; comparison and update preserve it. This explains more than a single successful example.
texts.cpp.telemetry.recap: Keep only the necessary state. Initialize a maximum from the first element and keep the preceding value for adjacent comparisons.
texts.cpp.telemetry.rises.explanation: Equal adjacent measurements do not count as a rise. A single measurement has no predecessor.

texts.cpp.telemetry.rises.hint.2: After comparing, always store current into previous.

texts.cpp.telemetry.rises.title: How many rises?

texts.cpp.telemetry.summary.explanation: One pass maintains two independent pieces of state. The average's divisor n is guaranteed to be nonzero.
texts.cpp.telemetry.summary.hint.1: Include the first value in both the sum and the maximum.
texts.cpp.telemetry.summary.hint.2: Process the remaining n-1 values in one loop; convert the sum before dividing.
texts.cpp.telemetry.summary.prompt: Input: n (1–100), then n integer readings from −100 to 100. Print the maximum and average, separated by a space, with two digits after the decimal point for the average.
texts.cpp.telemetry.summary.title: Expedition summary
texts.cpp.telemetry.theory:
You do not need to store every sequence in full. A sum needs an accumulator, a maximum needs the best value so far, and a count of rises needs the preceding measurement. These are streaming algorithms: read a new value, update the state, and move on.

Initialize the maximum of a nonempty sequence from its first value, not from zero: when every number is negative, zero is not their maximum. Compare adjacent measurements starting with the second one. The n≥1 contract makes it safe to read the first element separately.

The final task uses long long for the sum and floating-point division for the average.

At the ticket office, prices are conveniently stored as whole coins when the task does not require fractional monetary amounts. Read the input values first, calculate the cost and remaining payment next, then format the report. Do not mix input prompts into the required output.

This mini-project guarantees a sufficient budget, so no branching is needed. To handle arbitrary user input, you would need validation and decisions, which are upcoming topics. Distinguish task guarantees from language guarantees.

texts.cpp.types.microscope: Most decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly in binary floating point. Formatting a number to two decimal places does not turn calculations into exact monetary arithmetic. Real monetary amounts commonly use integer minor units or another deliberately chosen representation. Here, double is a learning model for measurements.

texts.cpp.types.temperature.title: Average temperature
texts.cpp.types.theory:
double stores numbers with a fractional part: double distance = 2.5;. In C++ source, use a dot as the decimal separator. int stores integers; converting double to int discards the fractional part towards zero, provided that the result is representable.

char marker = 'A'; stores one character code unit written in single quotation marks; "A" is a string literal, not a char. A Russian character usually occupies several bytes in UTF-8, so one char cannot be promised to hold any letter. bool ready = true; stores true or false. Without special formatting, printing a bool produces 1 or 0.

For a fixed number of decimal places, include <iomanip> and output std::fixed << std::setprecision(2). This changes stream formatting, not the stored number. Valid numeric input in these tasks uses a decimal dot.

This explains termination here. For negative integers, n>0 prevents the body from executing at all; do not extend the input contract without revisiting the algorithm.

texts.cpp.while.termination.choice.42c50507801: The condition stays true and the program keeps printing
texts.cpp.while.termination.explanation: An unchanged true condition causes unbounded repetition. Do not run this as a reference program.
texts.cpp.while.termination.hint.2: Check whether the body changes n.

texts.cpp.while.termination.title: A forgotten step
texts.cpp.while.theory:
while (condition) { ... } tests its condition before every iteration. It is useful when the repetition count is not known in advance. The body must change the state that controls continuation; otherwise the loop may run forever.

To process the digits of a positive n, take n%10 and remove the last digit using n/=10. The /= operator assigns the quotient back to the variable. Zero needs attention: while(n>0) does not execute for it. do { ... } while (condition); tests the condition after the body and executes at least once. This form requires a semicolon after while.

long long holds the larger integers used in these tasks; initial values and bounds must still be specified.
